translationRepairs: On guihai Heyang military commissioner Li Jilin came to court.
On guihai Hezhong military commissioner Li Jilin came to court.
Chinese 河中節度使 names the Hezhong circuit; Heyang (河陽) is a different command. The literal wrongly substitutes Heyang; Hezhong is the accurate replacement.

That day Heyang military commissioner, Guardian Grand Mentor, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Xiping Li Jilin was made Huazhou military commissioner; soon Zhu Shouyin was ordered to surround his residence with troops, execute him, and exterminate his clan.

That day Hezhong military commissioner, Guardian Grand Mentor, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Xiping Li Jilin was made Huazhou military commissioner; soon Zhu Shouyin was ordered to surround his residence with troops, execute him, and exterminate his clan.
The office string begins 河中節度使; rendering it Heyang misnames Li Jilin’s circuit. Replacing with Hezhong restores the Chinese place-name.
On jiashen Cunba of Yan became Heyang commissioner and Cunwo of Hua became Yan commissioner.
On jiashen Cunba of Yan became Hezhong commissioner and Cunwo of Hua became Yan commissioner.
Cunba is made 河中節度使, not 河陽. The idiomatic Heyang is a real toponym error; Hezhong is correct while leaving the existing Yan/Hua abbreviations untouched.
On jiashen Yanzhou military commissioner and Prince of Yong Cunba was made Heyang military commissioner; Huazhou military commissioner and Prince of Shen Cunwo was made Yanzhou military commissioner.

On jiashen Yanzhou military commissioner and Prince of Yong Cunba was made Hezhong military commissioner; Huazhou military commissioner and Prince of Shen Cunwo was made Yanzhou military commissioner.
Literal likewise turns 河中 into Heyang for Cunba’s appointment. Hezhong matches the Chinese; the rest of the sentence is already accurate.
On yiyou the palace woman Jing Cha said that when Emperor Zhaozong was killed, over a thousand royals were buried in three pits west of Longxing Temple and asked for reburial."

On yiyou, the palace woman Jing Cha submitted a report: "When Emperor Zhaozong met his end, more than a thousand members of the imperial clan were killed at the same time and buried in three pits north of the old Longxing Temple, west of the palace city. I request that they be reburied."
The complete repair restores both the location and the direct quotation structure of Jing Cha's report.
(The 《Ouyang History》 dates dinghai: Shi Wu, Xue Jingrong, Zhou Tangyin, Yang Shitai, Wang Jing, Lai Ren, and Bai Fengguo, Li Jilin's killers, were executed.)〉
(The 《Ouyang History》 dates dinghai: Shi Wu, Xue Jingrong, Zhou Tangyin, Yang Shitai, Wang Jing, Lai Ren, and Bai Fengguo, Li Jilin's generals, were executed.)〉

殺李繼麟之將 is kill Li Jilin’s generals (object 將 belonging to 李繼麟), not “his killers.” s0029–s0030 identify the same men as Youqian/Jilin’s old generals executed though innocent, confirming the generals reading.
(The 《Ouyang History》 records dinghai: the generals who killed Li Jilin—Shi Wu, Xue Jingrong, Zhou Tangyin, Yang Shitai, Wang Jing, Lai Ren, and Bai Fengguo—were executed.)〉
(The 《Ouyang History》 records dinghai: Li Jilin's generals—Shi Wu, Xue Jingrong, Zhou Tangyin, Yang Shitai, Wang Jing, Lai Ren, and Bai Fengguo—were executed.)〉
Literal “generals who killed Li Jilin” reverses agent and patient. 殺李繼麟之將 means the generals of Li Jilin were killed; the proposed “Li Jilin’s generals” is accurate.
After years on distant frontiers they were denied even a glimpse of family on returning to Beizhou.
After years on distant frontiers, cut off from home, when they were finally relieved and came within a stone's throw of home, they were still denied even a glimpse of their families.
Beizhou is invented; the Chinese says that after relief they came very near home. 'Within a stone's throw' renders 咫尺 idiomatically while preserving the denial of contact with their families.

Now a brilliant sovereign rules above and the realm is one family. The elite troops following the imperial carriage number no fewer than a million. Xiping has pacified Ba and Shu and awed Chinese and barbarians alike. You gentlemen each have families—why act like this!"

Now a brilliant sovereign rules above and the realm is one family. The elite troops following the imperial carriage number no fewer than a million. To the west Ba and Shu have been pacified, awing Chinese and barbarians alike. You gentlemen each have families—why act like this!"
西平巴、蜀 is westward pacification of Ba and Shu, not a proper name Xiping. The proposed rephrase matches the verbal sense and removes the invented agent.

Now a brilliant sovereign is above and the realm is one family; the following elite troops are not fewer than a million; Xiping has pacified Ba and Shu and awed China and barbarians—you each have families; why act thus!"

Now a brilliant sovereign is above and the realm is one family; the following elite troops are not fewer than a million; to the west Ba and Shu have been pacified, awing China and barbarians—you each have families; why act thus!"
Literal repeats the same Xiping misreading of 西平. “To the west Ba and Shu have been pacified” correctly takes 西 as direction and 平 as the verb.
He fled alone on horseback to the capital.
Chinese says 京師, the capital, without naming Luoyang. Replacing the invented city with “the capital” and keeping the flight-on-horseback sense is faithful.
Ren Yuan was sent to pursue him.
Ren Huan was sent to pursue him.
任圜 is Ren Huan (圜 = huán); Yuan is a wrong reading of the given name. The idiomatic repair restores the standard English form.
Deputy pacification commissioner Ren Yuan was sent to lead troops in pursuit.
Deputy pacification commissioner Ren Huan was sent to lead troops in pursuit.
Literal likewise misreads 圜 as Yuan. Ren Huan is the correct personal name for 任圜.
Cunba of Heyang, Prince of Yong, was ordered back to his fief.
Cunba of Hezhong, Prince of Yong, was ordered back to his fief.
詔河中節度使…存霸 names Hezhong, not Heyang. The idiomatic circuit label must be Hezhong.
An edict ordered Heyang military commissioner and Prince of Yong Cunba to return to his fief.
An edict ordered Hezhong military commissioner and Prince of Yong Cunba to return to his fief.
Literal repeats the Heyang error for 河中. Hezhong is the accurate circuit name for Cunba’s office.
With Kang Yanxiao holding Han, Jiji sent the central army under Ren Yuan while he stayed at Lizhou and could not return east.
With Kang Yanxiao holding Hanzhou, Jiji sent the central army under Ren Huan while he stayed at Lizhou and could not return east.
漢州 is Hanzhou, so that part of the proposal is right, but the after still keeps Ren Yuan for 任圜. The complete repair needs Hanzhou and Ren Huan.
On yisi Li Su of the Right Wuwei became salt commissioner for the Anyi and Jie pools; Li Qi of Revenue became state accounts commissioner.
On yisi Li Su of the Right Wuwei became salt commissioner for the Anyi and Jie pools; Li Qi of Personnel became state accounts commissioner.
吏部尚書 is Minister of Personnel; Revenue would be 戶部. Replacing Revenue with Personnel corrects the board title.
On yisi Right Wuwei upper general Li Su was made salt monopoly commissioner for Anyi and Jie counties' two pools; Minister of Revenue Li Qi was made state accounts commissioner.
On yisi Right Wuwei upper general Li Su was made salt monopoly commissioner for Anyi and Jie counties' two pools; Minister of Personnel Li Qi was made state accounts commissioner.
Literal “Minister of Revenue” likewise mistranslates 吏部尚書. Minister of Personnel is the correct office.

At dawn the mutinous army escorted Siyuan and Huo Yanwei into Ye, then was again coerced by Huangfu Hui, Zhao Jin, and the rest; Siyuan with deceitful words got out and at midnight reached Wei county.

At dawn the mutinous army escorted Siyuan and Huo Yanwei into Ye; they were again coerced by Huangfu Hui, Zhao Jin, and the rest; Siyuan with deceitful words got out and at midnight reached Wei county.

After 擁嗣源及霍彥威入於鄴城, 復為皇甫暉、趙進等所脅 has Siyuan and Huo Yanwei as the patients of coercion. The prior “then was again coerced” wrongly makes the mutinous army the patient; “they were again coerced” restores the Chinese subjects.
Cunxu sent Siyuan's son Congshen and envoy Bai Congxun with an edict; at Weizhou Xingqin shackled Congshen and they could not pass.
Cunxu sent Siyuan's son Congshen and envoy Bai Congxun with an edict; at Weizhou, Xingqin shackled Congshen and they could not pass.
Chinese separates place and agent: 行至衛州，從審為元行欽所械. Without the comma, “at Weizhou Xingqin” fuses place and person; the comma restores the readable boundary already present in the Chinese.

Cunxu called the chancellors to the informal hall; the empress brought out two silver dressing basins and three infant princes Mange and said, "Outsiders say the inner treasury is endless; tribute went out as fast as it came—now we have only dressing cases and infants—sell them for the army."

Cunxu called the chancellors to the informal hall; the empress brought out from the palace two dressing cases and two silver basins, together with three imperial sons, including Mange, and said to the ministers, "Outsiders say the inner treasury is endless; tribute went out as fast as it came—now we have only dressing cases and infants—sell them for the army."
妝奩銀盆各二 means two dressing cases and two silver basins. 皇子滿哥三人 means three imperial sons, including the named Mange, not one prince among three unspecified persons.

The Emperor summoned the chief ministers to the informal hall; the empress brought out from the palace two silver basins of her toilet case each and three infant princes Mange, and said to the chief ministers, "Outsiders say the inner treasury has countless gold and treasure; when the feudal lords presented tribute it was at once given away in grants—what the palace now has is only toilet cases and infants—sell them to supply the army."

The Emperor summoned the chief ministers to the informal hall; the empress brought out from the palace two dressing cases and two silver basins, together with three imperial sons, including Mange, and said to the chief ministers, "Outsiders say the inner treasury has countless gold and treasure; when the feudal lords presented tribute it was at once given away in grants—what the palace now has is only dressing cases and infants—sell them to supply the army."
The literal field requires the same correction: two of each object and three imperial sons, including Mange.
Ge and the rest withdrew in fear.
Dou Luge and the rest withdrew in fear.

革 here abbreviates 豆盧革 from the preceding minister scene. Bare “Ge” obscures the referent that the idiomatic already renders Dou Luge; expanding the abbreviation restores identification without changing sense.

You have served me in fortune and hardship and shared all without exception; now in this danger you should rely on your plans, yet in the end you are silent without words and sit watching success or failure.
You have served me in fortune and hardship and shared all without exception; now in this danger I rely on your plans, yet in the end you are silent without words and sit watching success or failure.
賴爾籌謀 has the speaker relying on the addressees’ plans (賴 + 爾籌謀). “You should rely on your plans” reverses the dependency; “I rely on your plans” matches the Chinese and the idiomatic.
On the dingchou new moon of the fourth month Prince Yong Cunba became northern capital regent and Prince Shen Cunwo Heyang commissioner.
On the dingchou new moon of the fourth month Prince Yong Cunba became northern capital regent and Prince Shen Cunwo Hezhong commissioner.
申王存渥為河中節度使 is Hezhong, not Heyang. The idiomatic circuit name must be corrected.
Fourth month, dingchou new moon: Prince of Yong Cunba was made northern capital regent and Prince of Shen Cunwo was made Heyang military commissioner.
Fourth month, dingchou new moon: Prince of Yong Cunba was made northern capital regent and Prince of Shen Cunwo was made Hezhong military commissioner.
Literal repeats Heyang for 河中. Hezhong is the correct military-commissioner title for Cunwo.

The historian writes: Zhuangzong rose with heroic purpose from the Yellow and Fen rivers and by force pacified Bian and Luo; he avenged his house and revived the dynasty—matching Shaokang's restoration of Xia or Guangwu's mandate, yet surpassing neither in praise.

The historian writes: Zhuangzong rose with heroic purpose from the Yellow and Fen rivers and by force pacified Bian and Luo; he avenged his house and revived the dynasty—even Shaokang's restoring Xia to match Heaven and Guangwu's receiving the mandate could not surpass it.

雖…亦無以加也 means even Shaokang’s and Guangwu’s restorations could not surpass Zhuangzong’s achievement. “Surpassing neither in praise” reverses the comparison; the proposal restores the correct direction.
Outside, eunuchs threw government into chaos; inside, the hen ruled the dawn.
Outside, actors threw government into chaos; inside, the hen ruled the dawn.
伶人 are court actors/entertainers, not eunuchs. The idiomatic agent of 亂政 must be actors.
Without, eunuchs disordering government; within, the hen crowing at dawn.
Without, actors disordering government; within, the hen crowing at dawn.
Literal likewise renders 伶人 as eunuchs. Actors is the accurate English for the Chinese term.
